about.title: About «PATH TO OPPORTUNITIES»
about.p1: «PATH TO OPPORTUNITIES | طريق الفرص» is a dedicated non-profit educational web discovery initiative aimed at enabling students and researchers across the Arab world to access trusted global educational opportunities.
about.p2: We uphold strict standards of transparency, web accessibility (WCAG 2.2), and student-centered UX. All published records display verified timelines, criteria, and official institutional sources.

guide.title: Application Guide for International Opportunities
guide.subtitle: Actionable guidelines and structured roadmaps to prepare standout academic and professional applications

roadmap.title: The Standout Application Roadmap
roadmap.step1Desc: Carefully check eligibility criteria, minimum GPA, and language requirements before investing time in an application.
roadmap.step2Desc: Establish a timeline marking application closing dates and schedule document preparation at least one month in advance.
roadmap.step3Desc: Translate certified transcripts and degree certificates through authorized translators and keep clear high-res PDFs.
roadmap.step4Desc: Draft an original, concise personal statement explaining your academic journey, future goals, and reasons for choosing this specific program.
roadmap.step5Desc: Reach out to your professors or mentors 4-6 weeks in advance to allow ample time for personalized reference letters.
roadmap.step6Desc: Proofread your application, verify all required attachments are in place, and submit at least two days before the deadline.

docs.title: Core Documents for Most Opportunities
docs.doc1Desc: Chronological, focused on academic accomplishments, projects, and skills relevant to the opportunity.
docs.doc2Desc: Articulates your genuine interest, background, and alignment with the program goals.
docs.doc3Desc: From academic professors or professional managers who have directly supervised your performance.
docs.doc4Desc: Officially translated and notarized according to the host institution's requirements.

tips.title: Golden Tips to Boost Acceptance Chances
tips.tip1Desc: Review committees evaluate thousands of submissions and spot generic templates immediately. Speak with authentic voice.
tips.tip2Desc: Tailoring 3 high-quality applications to specific programs is vastly more effective than blasting 20 generic submissions.
tips.tip3Desc: Grammar and typographical errors signal lack of care. Have a peer or academic advisor proofread your letters.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: Are IELTS / TOEFL test scores mandatory for all opportunities?
faq.a1: Not universally. Many universities accept an official English Proficiency Certificate if your prior degree was instructed in English. Check each institution's specific language policy.
faq.q2: What is the difference between full and partial funding?
faq.a2: Full funding typically covers tuition fees, a living stipend, travel allowances, and health insurance. Partial funding usually waives a portion of tuition only.
faq.q3: Can I apply before receiving my final graduation diploma?
faq.a3: Yes! Most degree programs allow final-year students to apply by submitting cumulative transcripts up to the latest completed semester alongside an expected graduation letter.
faq.q4: How far in advance should I start preparing my application?
faq.a4: Starting 2 to 3 months prior to the closing deadline is strongly recommended to gather recommendations, draft personal essays, and legalize documents without stress.
